mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real GDP growth above 3% for two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of sustained GDP acceleration above 3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when UNRATE is persistently below 5% for three months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained INDPRO decline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals robust household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both above 12-month moving average simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both RSAFS and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in CPI inflation below 1% for two consecutive months signals a disinflationary tightening, which reduces real interest rates and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL < 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of disinflationary tightening (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment above 200,000 new jobs per month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market absorption, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 200,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong payroll employment growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) for five consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.10).
